title: Microwindow handoff for reserved capacity smoothing and reset consistency
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Customers on Reserved capacity occasionally observe sudden token consumption cliffs and transient throttles during monthly/daily resets or when cross-region lease handoffs occur. Root causes include coarse month/day boundary resets, late-arriving usage events, and aggressive per-tenant burst buckets that are refilled at a single instant. Goal: Introduce a microwindow handoff model that slices reserved quotas into small contiguous micro-epochs (configurable, default 1 minute) and performs staggered, idempotent refill handoffs from global lease to tenant-local counters. The model should reduce perceived spike throttles, make resets tolerant to clock drift/late events, and enable graceful transient overdraft smoothing for reserved customers without changing billing semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Production rollout for 10% of reserved customers with must-not-increase-invoice: billing totals must remain within +/-0.05% of current accounting for the test window
End-to-end latency impact < 2ms median on token meter path for both hosted and dedicated deployments
Observed peak throttle incidents during boundary resets reduced by >= 80% for sampled tenants in canary cohort
Backfill and late-event reconciliation flow does not create duplicate credits; all handoffs are idempotent and logged
Dashboard and alerting: new metric `quota.microwindow.handoff_failures` and SLO on successful handoffs >= 99.9%
technical_approach: Design: split each reserved subscription's refilled quantum into N microwindows each with its own lightweight lease token. At reset time instead of a single refill event we schedule staggered handoffs: primary lease creates a sequence of micro-credits and writes a monotonic handoff cursor to the global ledger (strongly-consistent store). Tenants consume against their local microwindow counters; when a microwindow is exhausted the runtime attempts to atomically acquire the next micro-credit. Key properties: (1) idempotent acquire via compare-and-swap on monotonic cursor, (2) eventual reconciliation for late events by a backfill job that scans the handoff cursor and usage ledger to close gaps, (3) overdraft smoothing via temporary soft-borrow lane limited by a configurable policy per customer and reconciled before invoice close. Implementation: extend meter pipeline (meter-proxy + quota-service) to support microwindow tokens, add a compact microwindow cache in serving runtime keyed by tenant+window, and a handoff coordinator service that exposes /acquire-microcredit and /reconcile endpoints. Storage: leverage existing strongly-consistent ledger (Postgres row-level CAS) for cursor writes and Redis for short-lived microwindow state. Rollout: feature flag guarded, staged canary, and per-tenant opt-out. Telemetry: emit handoff latency histograms and acquire success rates. Backout: a global feature flag to disable microwindowing and fall back to the current refill path.
risks: Increased complexity in the meter path could add tail latency if caching is ineffective
Edge cases around DST/timezone-aligned billing windows and cross-region failover need careful testing
Incorrect reconciliation may cause subtle double-counting or understatement if backfill mistakes are made
Operational burden: new runbooks and debugging flows required for on-call responders
notes: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting with Billing, Runtime, and Observability. Decided default microwindow size = 60s with future tunability.
2026-02-26: Prototype implemented in meter-proxy; initial bench shows median add path +1.1ms. Markus to optimize local cache first.
2026-03-02: Design review feedback (from Lina M. and DevOps): prefer Postgres-based cursor CAS for strong correctness; agreed to Redis as ephemeral cache only.
2026-03-05: Security review requested for the reconcile job; initial answers: no extra PII, KMS not required (job runs under billing role).
2026-03-07: Load test (canary-size workload) passed functional criteria but saw 2.6ms p95 on meter path under synthetic spikes; proposed mitigations: increase cache TTL and prefetch next microcredit.
2026-03-10: Finalized telemetry dims and added `quota.microwindow.cursor_lag` to track reconciliation lag. Preparing PR for meter-proxy and quota-service.
release_plan: 1) Feature-flagged unit/integration tests -> 2) Internal canary (10% reserved tenants) for 48h -> 3) Monitor metrics and reconcile job for 7 days -> 4) Gradual ramp to 50%/100% with alarms and automated rollback on handoff_failure spike
oncall_runbook: If `quota.microwindow.handoff_failures` > 0.5% for 10min: 1) enable global feature-flag fallback, 2) re-run reconcile job for last 24h, 3) notify billing-eng@redwood.ai, 4) open incident and escalate to Markus/Asheesh
